title: How a browser cache reuses one response
purpose: See when a stored response is reused, revalidated with a 304, or fetched again from the origin.
sequence_reason: A cached response changes state as time passes, from missing to fresh to stale, so motion shows each step and its cause.
summary: A browser asks for app.css. The first request misses and the cache stores the 200 response with max-age=60 and an ETag. At 30 seconds the copy is fresh and the cache answers alone. At 90 seconds the copy is stale, so the cache sends If-None-Match and the origin answers 304, which keeps the stored body.
explanation: A cache reuses a stored copy while its lifetime is greater than its age. After that it asks the origin, and a 304 answer keeps the copy.

learning_check.question: A copy has max-age=60 and is 90 seconds old. What does the cache send before it reuses the copy?
learning_check.answer: A conditional request with If-None-Match and the stored ETag. A 304 answer lets it reuse the stored body.

scenes.heading: One stylesheet, one cache
scenes.narration: A cache keeps a copy of a response. Watch one browser cache reuse app.css.

scenes.heading: First request: a miss
scenes.narration: The first request finds no stored copy. The cache forwards it to the origin and stores the 200 response with its headers.

scenes.heading: Fresh means lifetime is greater than age
scenes.narration: A stored copy is fresh while its lifetime is greater than its age. Here max-age gives a lifetime of sixty seconds.

terms.note: seconds since the origin made the response

scenes.heading: At 30 seconds: a fresh hit
scenes.narration: At thirty seconds the age is thirty, so the copy is fresh. The cache answers alone, with no trip to the origin.

scenes.heading: At 90 seconds: stale, so ask first
scenes.narration: At ninety seconds the copy is stale. The cache asks the origin with If-None-Match. A 304 answer means keep your copy.

scenes.heading: 304 or 200 after a revalidation
scenes.narration: A 304 sends only headers, so the cache reuses the stored body. A 200 sends a new body that replaces the copy.

left.label: 304 Not Modified
items: The cache reuses the stored body

right.label: 200 OK
items: A new body crosses the network
The new response replaces the copy

visual.verdict: Validation is a cheap question: has it changed?
